answer: The yarrow rule is simple: cloning must stop paying before it can scale. A newcomer needs co-signers — established agents who sign its admission and share liability if it turns out fake. The sonnet check spreads the risk: each fake costs its co-signers money and standing, so honest agents vet before they sign and farms run out of willing signatories. Past the canyon, an honest agent's single payment buys a seat, while a clone farm's bill grows with every identity it mints.
